entries.feature: The dashboard composition is specified: four core panels (CPU aggregate, memory/swap, disk, network) in at most two semantic groups above the unchanged searchable process table and inspector, divided by a standard Split (the user decided on 2026-11-27 that Split, PX-070-G02, is a required prerequisite: "Draggable divider (Recommended)"); compact, expanded and hidden presentations as saved semantic choices with moves-only layout changes and scalar-only samples; compact CPU and memory/swap reuse the PX-070 meters; bounded panel and device-expansion controls; local window, divider and graph resizing that sends nothing; keyboard focus order and PX-016-G01 focus shortcuts; host/account/incarnation only in PX-095 client chrome; disconnected presentation through PX-022-G01/PX-022-G02 and paused presentation through PX-015; PX-073-G01 depends on PX-095 for the host labels; later per-CPU, temperature and GPU panels never block the core four

Every required panel has a collector owner (existing procfs/summary for CPU and memory/swap, PX-054, PX-055, PX-056, PX-090), a renderer owner (existing Text, Progress, Row/Column and model-backed Table; PX-073 over PX-071/PX-072 for graphs; PX-070-G02 for Split), a unit policy (one-decimal shares with denominators, IEC bytes, IEC bytes per second, never bits), a freshness policy (own sample time and interval per panel, no implied atomic host snapshot, warming-up/unavailable/denied/not-provided/none-configured/collector-error/stale/paused states that never become zero, labelled gaps), a finite budget (nodes that do not grow with device expansion because one PX-071 graph node per panel carries up to 18 series, rows, series, 900 samples or 15 minutes per series, a fallback of 60 samples of at most 64 bytes per series, PX-090 history of 4 processes x 4 series, DASHBOARD_RESERVE_BYTES 1,179,648 and HISTORY_RESERVE_BYTES 458,752 summing every series, fallback row, device row and node a snapshot carries, which lowers PX-070's measured widest-row ceiling from 25,564 to 23,055 rows, and a 4 KiB/s steady-state payload bound) and a sentence-level accessible fallback with a fallback sample table covering the history of every shown series, per device included

Generic widget and profile support was reviewed against the checkout (registry.yaml node types and properties, server-rust/sdk widgets, ControlFactory.makeHandle, ExtensionMountResolver, capability.rs): graphs are missing and already owned by PX-071-PX-073; the standard Split container is in the registry but has no SDK builder, no renderer and no axis property, so it becomes the new prerequisite PX-070-G02 (ticket file, task-index entry, master plan, queue and catalogue, execution order after PX-070-G01) and PX-073-G01 now depends on it; the user approved planning its split_axis/SplitAxis registry property on 2026-11-27 ("Plan split_axis (Recommended)"), and the registry change itself still needs recorded user approval when PX-070-G02 is implemented; PX-071 now depends on PX-070-G01 and must let one graph node carry several series; PX-073-G01 now depends on PX-095; Tabs are not needed; accessibility grouping of labelled containers is left for PX-073-G01 to verify

entries.feature: An objective evaluation protocol is fixed before implementation: one matched Linux environment, the pinned btop binary checked against its digest, the same SSH relay at 0/100/300/600 ms, identical explicit 1 s and 2 s intervals, only fields both tools show with normalized units, owned bounded workloads with harness reference values, and four tasks (locate a busy process, inspect a trend, inspect disk/network activity, recover after disconnect) with numeric pass/fail criteria for the dashboard run by automation, keyboard-only and VoiceOver without graphs; btop is observed, never scored; no conclusion from screenshots; R1 (PX-027) and safe termination (PX-031) have no dashboard ticket in their transitive dependencies
